column3: Item
Child vocalizes while looking at the task materials.
Child smiles or laughs during the episode.
Child attempts to make eye contact with caregiver.
Child initiates interaction with caregiver spontaneously.
Child attempts to elicit caregiver's response.
Child displays strong reaction during the interaction.
Child gazes at caregiver's face or task materials after caregiver's non-verbal behaviours.
Child looks at caregiver's face or eyes when caregiver attempts eye contact.
Child vocalises or babbles within five seconds after caregiver's verbalisation.
Child vocalises or babbles within five seconds of caregiver's gestures, touch, or changes in facial expression.
Child gives, shows, or points to task material to share emotion with caregiver.
Child looks at caregiver's face to gather information/gain understanding.
Child vocalises or adjusts own behaviour within five seconds in response to caregiver's verbalisation.
Child smiles at caregiver within five seconds of caregiver's verbalisation.
Child behaves within five seconds in accord with caregiver's gestures, touch, or changes in expression.
Child widens eyes and/or shows postural attention to task situation.
Child becomes appropriately active in response to task situation.
Child's movements are clearly directed toward/away from the task or task material.
Child make clearly recognisable hand motions towards task materials during the episode.
Child is neither restless nor overactive.
Child stop displaying distress cues without caregiver's response.
Child stops displaying distress cues without caregiver's soothing attempts.
Child stops displaying distress cues within 15 seconds after caregiver's soothing attempts.
Child asks caregiver for help or consolation.
Child is not startled by caregiver's movements or changes in his/her facial expression.
Caregiver allows child to explore task material for at least five seconds before providing first task related instruction.
Caregiver pauses when child initiates behaviours during episode.
Caregiver asks for no more than three repetitions when child is successful at completing the task.
Caregiver does not physically force child to complete task.
Caregiver halts the episode when child is distressed.
After giving instructions, caregiver allows at least five seconds for child to attempt task before intervening.
Caregiver allows non-task manipulation of task materials after the original presentation.
Caregiver does not make critical or negative comments about child's task performance.
Caregiver encourages and/or allows child to perform task at least once before intervening.
Caregiver positions child to safely support it.
Caregiver provides an environment free of distractions.
Caregiver positions child so it can reach and manipulate materials.
Caregiver seeks the child's attention before beginning the task, at the outset of the teaching interaction.
Caregiver gives instructions only when the child is attentive (90% of the time).
Caregiver positions child so eye contact is possible during the teaching period (60%).
Caregiver changes position of child and/or materials after unsuccessful attempts by the child to do the task.
Caregiver keeps child in visual range.
Caregiver stays close to child and pays good attention.
Caregiver praises child's efforts at least once during the episode.
Caregiver emits positive, sympathetic, or soothing verbalisations.
Caregiver smiles or touches child within five seconds after child's smile or vocalisation.
Caregiver emits soothing non-verbal response (i.e. pat, touch, rock, caress, kiss).
Caregiver diverts the child by playing games, introducing new toy.
Caregiver does not vocalise to the child while the child is vocalises.
Caregiver verbally praises child during the episode.
Caregiver smiles and/or nods at the child.
Caregiver responds to child's vocalisations with affectionate verbal response.
Caregiver focuses own attention and child's attention on task during most of the episode.
Caregiver describes perceptual qualities of task materials to child.
Caregiver uses least two different sentences or phrases to describe task to child.
Caregiver uses explanatory verbal style more than imperative style in episode.
Caregiver's instructions are clear and unambiguous.
Caregiver uses both verbal description and non-verbal instruction.
Caregiver uses teaching loops (alerting, instruction, performance, and feedback) in instructing child.
Caregiver signals completion of task to child verbally or non-verbally.
Length of caregiver instruction to child is age appropriate.
Caregiver does not make negative comments to the child.
Caregiver does not yell at the child.
Caregiver does not use abrupt movements or rough handling.
Caregiver does not slap, hit, or spank.
Caregiver does not make negative comments to observer about the child.
Caregiver's body posture is relaxed during the episode.
Caregiver places him/herself in a face-to-face position with the child when talking to the child.
Caregiver behaves affectionately to child during the episode.
Caregiver makes constructive or encouraging statements to the child during episode.
